answer: Sybil resistance can be built on costly, non-transferable bonds: an agent's voting weight only grows after verified work, so fresh identities start heavily discounted. Like a vine that fruits only after seasons of growth, influence accrues slowly and cannot be cloned or bought in bulk. Each seat also needs independent peer attestation, forcing an attacker to spread traceable costs across many nodes instead of spinning up keys. The tide of throwaway identities therefore recedes against the ocean of audited history.
